course_sections_nonlecture_cohort.name: course_sections_nonlecture_cohort
course_sections_nonlecture_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE` AS `MEET_PLACE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID` AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
WHERE COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_LECTURE_SECTION`, '') <> 'Y'
  AND COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_LAB_SECTION`, '') <> 'Y'
  AND COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_RECITATION_SECTION`, '') <> 'Y'
  AND COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_DESIGN_SECTION`, '') <> 'Y'
  -- keep only rows that have a section identifier (grain) and represent offered sections/activities
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID`) <> ''
course_sections_nonlecture_cohort.description: One-row-per-section/independent-activity cohort filtered to exclude lecture/lab/recitation/design sections; keeps section identifiers, meeting place, responsible faculty id/name, term/effective term info, and subject title fields for downstream joins and filters.

catalog_subject_key_preference.name: catalog_subject_key_preference
catalog_subject_key_preference.body_sql:
SELECT
  `SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID,
  `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  `SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  CASE
    WHEN `SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL AND `SECTION_ID` <> '' THEN 'SECTION_ID'
    WHEN `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL AND `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` <> '' THEN 'MASTER_SUBJECT_ID'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS preferred_source,
  -- canonical subject_key: prefer SECTION_ID when present else MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
  CASE
    WHEN `SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL AND `SECTION_ID` <> '' THEN `SECTION_ID`
    WHEN `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL AND `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` <> '' THEN `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
    ELSE NULL
  END AS subject_key
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
catalog_subject_key_preference.description: Normalize a preferred subject key per catalog row: prefer SECTION_ID when present, otherwise use MASTER_SUBJECT_ID. Exposes canonical subject_key and flags which source column was used. One row per course_catalog_subject_offered row.

employee_office_location_parsed.name: employee_office_location_parsed
employee_office_location_parsed.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.`MIT_ID` AS MIT_ID,
  d.`FULL_NAME` AS FULL_NAME,
  d.`OFFICE_LOCATION` AS OFFICE_LOCATION,
  d.`OFFICE_PHONE` AS OFFICE_PHONE,
  b.`BUILDING_KEY` AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.`BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS` AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS
FROM
  `drupal_employee_directory` d
LEFT JOIN
  `buildings` b
    ON (
      -- Try to match on building number extracted from OFFICE_LOCATION when OFFICE_LOCATION contains a building number at start like "32-123" or "32-100"
      -- Extract pattern: leading digits (1-4) optionally followed by a dash and more digits/letters, match against BUILDING_NUMBER
      CASE
        WHEN d.`OFFICE_LOCATION` REGEXP '^[[:space:]]*[0-9]{1,4}([-][A-Za-z0-9]+)?' THEN
          TRIM(BOTH ' ' FROM SUBSTRING_INDEX(TRIM(d.`OFFICE_LOCATION`), ' ', 1))
        ELSE NULL
      END = b.`BUILDING_NUMBER`
    )

semantic_filters.NONE: No intrinsic filters; do not bake ADDRESS_PURPOSE or specific FULL_NAME into view

employee_office_location_parsed.description: Join-like projection intended to support mapping an employee's OFFICE_LOCATION text to room/floor/building; returns parsed components from OFFICE_LOCATION string where possible. One row per employee (MIT_ID).

section_format_and_enrollment.name: section_format_and_enrollment
section_format_and_enrollment.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  cso.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  cso.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.IS_LECTURE_SECTION AS IS_LECTURE_SECTION,
  cso.IS_LAB_SECTION AS IS_LAB_SECTION,
  cso.IS_RECITATION_SECTION AS IS_RECITATION_SECTION,
  cso.IS_DESIGN_SECTION AS IS_DESIGN_SECTION,
  -- Aggregate the format flags into a single pipe-separated FORMATS string in a stable order.
  TRIM(BOTH '|' FROM CONCAT(
    CASE WHEN cso.IS_LECTURE_SECTION IS NOT NULL AND cso.IS_LECTURE_SECTION <> '' AND UPPER(cso.IS_LECTURE_SECTION) NOT IN ('0','FALSE','N') THEN '|LECTURE' ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN cso.IS_LAB_SECTION IS NOT NULL AND cso.IS_LAB_SECTION <> '' AND UPPER(cso.IS_LAB_SECTION) NOT IN ('0','FALSE','N') THEN '|LAB' ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN cso.IS_RECITATION_SECTION IS NOT NULL AND cso.IS_RECITATION_SECTION <> '' AND UPPER(cso.IS_RECITATION_SECTION) NOT IN ('0','FALSE','N') THEN '|RECITATION' ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN cso.IS_DESIGN_SECTION IS NOT NULL AND cso.IS_DESIGN_SECTION <> '' AND UPPER(cso.IS_DESIGN_SECTION) NOT IN ('0','FALSE','N') THEN '|DESIGN' ELSE '' END
  )) AS FORMATS
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cso
section_format_and_enrollment.description: One row per section (SECTION_ID + TERM_CODE + SUBJECT_ID) aggregating format flags into a single FORMATS string and exposing enrollment counts (raw) if enrollment column is available in other chunk tables; here we expose format indicators to be combined with enrollment source later.

building_employee_counts.name: building_employee_counts
building_employee_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_NAME,
  b.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
  -- employee count per building: count of employee_directory rows whose OFFICE_LOCATION matches building number
  -- expose as EMPLOYEE_COUNT so view can be joined and used for metrics
  COALESCE(ed.emp_count, 0) AS EMPLOYEE_COUNT
FROM buildings AS b
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    OFFICE_LOCATION,
    COUNT(*) AS emp_count
  FROM employee_directory
  WHERE OFFICE_LOCATION IS NOT NULL AND OFFICE_LOCATION <> ''
  GROUP BY OFFICE_LOCATION
) AS ed
  ON ed.OFFICE_LOCATION = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
building_employee_counts.description: One row per building exposing building identifier plus an employee-count measure. Designed to be joined to building metadata; expects an employee-count column or reachable table with employee counts for buildings.

buildings_row_cohort.name: buildings_row_cohort

SELECT

  `buildings`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`

  AND TRIM(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER`) <> ''
  AND CAST(TRIM(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER`) AS SIGNED) = CAST(TRIM(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER`) AS DECIMAL)

buildings_normalized_counters.name: buildings_normalized_counters
buildings_normalized_counters.body_sql:
SELECT
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NAME` AS BUILDING_NAME,
  CAST(NULLIF(TRIM(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER`), '') AS SIGNED) AS BUILDING_COUNTER,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS BUILDING_KEY
FROM `buildings`
WHERE
  -- remove NULLs and empty strings
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER`) <> ''
  -- ensure the counter is a valid integer representation: optional leading +/-, digits only after trim
  AND TRIM(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER`) REGEXP '^[+-]?[0-9]+$'
buildings_normalized_counters.description: Normalized building rows with BUILDING_COUNTER cast to an integer column (where possible) and invalid/non-numeric counters removed. Keeps building key and name for joins and presentation.

iap_subject_offerings_rowlevel.name: iap_subject_offerings_rowlevel
iap_subject_offerings_rowlevel.body_sql:
SELECT
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` AS `HASS_ATTRIBUTE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE` AS `MEET_PLACE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME` AS `MEET_TIME`
FROM
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`
WHERE
  -- only include rows flagged as offered in IAP (IS_OFFERED_IAP expected 'Y' or similar non-null flag)
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` IS NOT NULL
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` <> ''
  -- required measure/key columns must be present (exclude NULL or empty-string)
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` IS NOT NULL
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` <> ''
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` IS NOT NULL
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` <> ''
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` <> ''
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` <> ''
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE` IS NOT NULL
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE` <> ''
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME` IS NOT NULL
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME` <> ''
iap_subject_offerings_rowlevel.description: One row per subject-offering/section that is flagged as offered in IAP, with raw enrollment and fee-related columns (no aggregation). Filters out rows missing academic year, category name, enrollment, or fee values; casts/normalizes empty strings to NULL are left to downstream queries but rows with NULLs in key measure columns are excluded at selection time to simplify downstream aggregation.

iap_subject_catalog_normalized.name: iap_subject_catalog_normalized
iap_subject_catalog_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT

iap_subject_catalog_normalized.description: Canonical information about subjects (subject id, subject code, titles, HASS/IAP category) at the subject (course) level. One row per subject (master subject id). Useful to count distinct subjects per category/year and to join with enrollment/fee tables.

iap_category_year_agg_prejoin.name: iap_category_year_agg_prejoin
iap_category_year_agg_prejoin.body_sql:

iap_category_year_agg_prejoin.description: Pre-aggregated counts of distinct subjects per IAP category + academic year based solely on course-catalog/subject-offered data present in this chunk. This view is grouped at the category+academic_year level and returns the number of distinct master subjects and the number of offering sections. Monetary and enrollment measures are intentionally omitted here because fee/enrollment columns are not present in this schema chunk; downstream query will join enrollment/fee tables and compute sums/min/max.

session_rows_with_iap_indicator.name: session_rows_with_iap_indicator
session_rows_with_iap_indicator.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID,
  cso.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  cso.`FALL_INSTRUCTORS` AS FALL_INSTRUCTORS,
  cso.`SPRING_INSTRUCTORS` AS SPRING_INSTRUCTORS,
  cso.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` AS IS_OFFERED_IAP,
  cso.`TERM_DURATION` AS TERM_DURATION,
  cso.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
  cso.`MEET_TIME` AS MEET_TIME,
  cso.`MEET_PLACE` AS MEET_PLACE,
  cso.`LAST_ACTIVITY_DATE` AS LAST_ACTIVITY_DATE,
  cso.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  cso.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  cso.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  cso.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  -- Derive a simple boolean-like indicator for "is IAP" without inventing stored columns:
  -- If the course explicitly marks IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y' (or '1'), or TERM_DURATION contains 'IAP',
  -- or TERM_CODE looks like an IAP term (lifted out of view logic; literals should be handled at query-time),
  -- produce a flag. Keep raw source columns above for downstream use.
  (CASE
     WHEN cso.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` IN ('Y','1','y','t','T','yes','YES') THEN 1
     WHEN cso.`TERM_DURATION` IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(cso.`TERM_DURATION`) LIKE '%iap%' THEN 1
     WHEN cso.`TERM_CODE` IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(cso.`TERM_CODE`) LIKE 'iap%' THEN 1
     ELSE 0
   END) AS IAP_INDICATOR
FROM
  `course_catalog_subject_offered` AS cso
-- No filtering here: view represents session/course-level rows. Keep one row per SECTION_ID.
session_rows_with_iap_indicator.description: Select rows that appear to represent individual course/session offerings and mark whether they are IAP offerings based on any term/term-duration/IS_OFFERED_IAP-like column. Keep raw session-level columns such as sponsor name, enrollment, fee, and has_session_info for downstream aggregation.

course_catalog_session_sponsor_and_measu.name: course_catalog_session_sponsor_and_measures
course_catalog_session_sponsor_and_measu.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- identity / grain
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,

  -- required raw columns (kept from source table as requested)
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`FALL_INSTRUCTORS` AS `FALL_INSTRUCTORS`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SPRING_INSTRUCTORS` AS `SPRING_INSTRUCTORS`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` AS `IS_OFFERED_IAP`,

  -- canonicalized sponsor name: course_catalog_subject_offered has no explicit sponsor column,
  -- so expose NULL as SPONSOR_NAME (do not substitute from other tables)
  NULL AS `SPONSOR_NAME`,

  -- canonical numeric measures: attempt to coerce known numeric-ish columns to integers.
  -- course_catalog_subject_offered stores LECTURE_UNITS, LAB_UNITS, PREPARATION_UNITS, TOTAL_UNITS as ints,
  -- keep them as-is but cast to signed to ensure numeric type in view.
  CAST(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`LECTURE_UNITS` AS SIGNED) AS `LECTURE_UNITS`,
  CAST(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`LAB_UNITS` AS SIGNED) AS `LAB_UNITS`,
  CAST(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`PREPARATION_UNITS` AS SIGNED) AS `PREPARATION_UNITS`,
  CAST(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TOTAL_UNITS` AS SIGNED) AS `TOTAL_UNITS`,

  -- enrollment / fee canonicalization: course_catalog_subject_offered does not have explicit FEE or ENROLLMENT fields named generically.
  -- It does have no direct numeric 'FEE' column; expose NULLs rather than deriving.
  NULL AS `ENROLLMENT_NUMBER`,
  NULL AS `FEE`,

  -- canonical HAS_SESSION_INFO flag: normalize common textual flags into 'Y'/'N'/NULL.
  -- Use raw IS_OFFERED_IAP as proxy for whether there may be IAP session info but do NOT substitute.
  -- Since course_catalog_subject_offered has no HAS_SESSION_INFO, return computed value based strictly on IS_OFFERED_IAP presence:
  CASE
    WHEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(LOWER(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP`)) IN ('y','yes','true','1') THEN 'Y'
    WHEN TRIM(LOWER(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP`)) IN ('n','no','false','0') THEN 'N'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `HAS_SESSION_INFO`

FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
course_catalog_session_sponsor_and_measu.description: Normalize/clean session-level sponsor and numeric measure fields from course_catalog_subject_offered: canonicalize sponsor name field(s) into SPONSOR_NAME, canonical enrollment and fee fields (cast to numeric where available), and canonical HAS_SESSION_INFO flag. Keeps one row per SECTION_ID.

term_codes_and_descriptions.name: term_codes_and_descriptions
term_codes_and_descriptions.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(at.TERM_CODE, ata.TERM_CODE) AS TERM_CODE,
  COALESCE(at.TERM_DESCRIPTION, ata.TERM_DESCRIPTION) AS TERM_DESCRIPTION,
  COALESCE(at.TERM_START_DATE, ata.TERM_START_DATE) AS TERM_START_DATE,
  COALESCE(at.TERM_END_DATE, ata.TERM_END_DATE) AS TERM_END_DATE
FROM academic_terms at
RIGHT JOIN academic_terms_all ata
  ON ata.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE
-- ensure every TERM_CODE present once: take TERM_CODE from academic_terms when present, otherwise from academic_terms_all
GROUP BY COALESCE(at.TERM_CODE, ata.TERM_CODE),
         COALESCE(at.TERM_DESCRIPTION, ata.TERM_DESCRIPTION),
         COALESCE(at.TERM_START_DATE, ata.TERM_START_DATE),
         COALESCE(at.TERM_END_DATE, ata.TERM_END_DATE)
term_codes_and_descriptions.description: Mapping of term code to canonical term description and term date range using academic_terms (fallback to academic_terms_all if needed). One row per TERM_CODE.

iap_location_meettimes_normalized.name: iap_location_meettimes_normalized
iap_location_meettimes_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  -- preferred canonical MEET_PLACE taken from course_catalog_subject_offered
  cso.MEET_PLACE AS MEET_PLACE,
  -- keep raw meet time strings from course_catalog_subject_offered
  cso.MEET_TIME AS MEET_TIME,
  -- also expose the drupal source SECTION_ID / MEET_PLACE / MEET_TIME for downstream comparison
  dcc.SECTION_ID AS drupal_SECTION_ID,
  dcc.MEET_PLACE AS drupal_MEET_PLACE,
  dcc.MEET_TIME AS drupal_MEET_TIME,
  -- master subject id from cis_course_catalog (may be NULL)
  cis.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cso
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog dcc
  ON dcc.SECTION_ID = cso.SECTION_ID
LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog cis
  ON cis.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
WHERE cso.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY cso.SECTION_ID, cso.MEET_PLACE, cso.MEET_TIME, dcc.SECTION_ID, dcc.MEET_PLACE, dcc.MEET_TIME, cis.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
iap_location_meettimes_normalized.description: Normalized projection of meeting place, canonical MEET_PLACE value, parsed SESSION_START_TIME and SESSION_END_TIME tokens (kept as raw strings here) and a normalized fee column placeholder. One row per section/SECTION_ID + MEET_PLACE combination to support duration calculation and fee summation later. This view does light cleaning and selects preferred columns from available tables.

sis_course_subjects.name: sis_course_subjects

SELECT

sis_subject_row_level.name: sis_subject_row_level
sis_subject_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- cis_course_catalog source columns (preserve names, alias to bare column names)
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`                               AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`                        AS `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE`                             AS `SUBJECT_CODE`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`                           AS `SUBJECT_NUMBER`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`                          AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`                          AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`                            AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,

  -- course_catalog_subject_offered source columns (qualified to ensure exact sourcing)
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`                   AS `SUBJECT_ID_ccso`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`            AS `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_ccso`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_CODE`                 AS `SUBJECT_CODE_ccso`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`               AS `SUBJECT_NUMBER_ccso`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`              AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE_ccso`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`              AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME_ccso`,

  -- drupal_course_catalog source columns
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`                            AS `SUBJECT_ID_drupal`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`                     AS `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_drupal`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE`                          AS `SUBJECT_CODE_drupal`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`                        AS `SUBJECT_NUMBER_drupal`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`                       AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE_drupal`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`                       AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME_drupal`

FROM `cis_course_catalog`
-- left join to course_catalog_subject_offered to bring its exact stored subject fields when available
LEFT JOIN `course_catalog_subject_offered`
  ON `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
     OR `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`
     OR `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
-- left join to drupal_course_catalog to bring its exact stored subject fields when available
LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog`
  ON `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `drupal_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
     OR `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`
     OR `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = `drupal_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`

course_offerings_current_term.name: course_offerings_current_term

subject_iap_session_counts.name: subject_iap_session_counts
subject_iap_session_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  cso.SUBJECT_TITLE AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  cso.HASS_ATTRIBUTE AS HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  cso.IS_OFFERED_IAP AS IS_OFFERED_IAP,
  cso.TERM_DURATION AS TERM_DURATION,
  cso.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  cso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  cso.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  -- count of valid session rows for this subject: must have non-empty MEET_TIME and a SECTION_ID
  COUNT(
    CASE
      WHEN cso.MEET_TIME IS NOT NULL
       AND TRIM(cso.MEET_TIME) <> ''
       AND cso.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL
       AND TRIM(cso.SECTION_ID) <> ''
      THEN 1
      ELSE NULL
    END
  ) AS VALID_SESSION_COUNT
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered AS cso
GROUP BY
  cso.SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.SUBJECT_CODE,
  cso.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  cso.HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  cso.IS_OFFERED_IAP,
  cso.TERM_DURATION,
  cso.TERM_CODE,
  cso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  cso.SECTION_ID
subject_iap_session_counts.description: Aggregate count of valid sessions per subject restricted to session rows (one row per subject). This view counts only session rows that include a non-empty MEET_TIME (start/end must be parsed at question time) and that have SECTION_ID. Does not apply IAP literal filters so it can be reused for other term-duration counts.

subject_level_indicators.name: subject_level_indicators
subject_level_indicators.body_sql:
SELECT
  `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS `SUBJECT_CODE`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION` AS `SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  -- derived indicator: IS_GRADUATE_LEVEL when a graduate-level flag/column is present.
  -- CIS source does not have an explicit IS_GRADUATE_LEVEL column in schema; attempt to infer
  -- conservatively from GRADE_TYPE or SUBJECT_ID patterns is not allowed by rules.
  -- Therefore expose NULL so downstream consumers know it's unavailable from CIS.
  NULL AS `IS_GRADUATE_LEVEL`
FROM
  `cis_course_catalog`
subject_level_indicators.description: Normalize/derive indicators about subject-level attributes (e.g., whether offered at graduate level) from course-catalog flags/columns. This view produces one row per subject (MASTER_SUBJECT_ID or SUBJECT_ID) with canonical SUBJECT_CODE, SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION, DEPARTMENT_NAME and a derived IS_GRADUATE_LEVEL flag when detectable.

department_subject_course_counts.name: department_subject_course_counts
department_subject_course_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  c.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  c.`SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION` AS SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION,
  c.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(
      COALESCE(s.`SECTION_ID`, ''), '||',
      COALESCE(c.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`, ''), '||',
      COALESCE(c.`SUBJECT_ID`, '')
  )) AS canonical_course_count
FROM
  `cis_course_catalog` c
LEFT JOIN
  `subject_offered` s
  ON s.`TERM_CODE` = c.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`
    AND s.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = c.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
    AND s.`SUBJECT_ID` = c.`SUBJECT_ID`
GROUP BY
  c.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  c.`SUBJECT_CODE`,
  c.`SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION`,
  c.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
department_subject_course_counts.description: Aggregated counts of distinct canonical courses per department+subject. Uses canonical_course_id (deduped from SECTION_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_ID) to count unique courses. One row per department + SIS subject code.

course_material_row_level.name: course_material_row_level
course_material_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  `cis`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `ccso`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,
  `drupal`.`SECTION_ID` AS `drupal_SECTION_ID`,
  `drupal`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `drupal_SUBJECT_ID`,
  `drupal`.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS `SUBJECT_CODE`,
  -- material / author fields to allow downstream author-splitting; filter will remove empty authors
  `tipm`.`AUTHOR` AS `AUTHOR`,
  `tipm`.`TITLE` AS `TITLE`,
  `libcat`.`CATALOG_AUTHOR_NAME` AS `CATALOG_AUTHOR_NAME`,
  `libcat`.`CATALOG_TITLE` AS `CATALOG_TITLE`,
  `libmatstat`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS `LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS`,
  `tipmatstat`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS `TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS`,
  -- carry keys so view remains joinable
  `tip`.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` AS `TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`,
  `tip`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` AS `TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`,
  `tip`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` AS `TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`,
  `ccso`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID_for_grain_check`
FROM `cis_course_catalog` AS `cis`
LEFT JOIN `course_catalog_subject_offered` AS `ccso`
  ON `cis`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `ccso`.`SUBJECT_ID`
LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog` AS `drupal`
  ON `drupal`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `cis`.`SUBJECT_ID`
LEFT JOIN `tip_subject_offered` AS `tipso`
  ON `tipso`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `cis`.`SUBJECT_ID`
LEFT JOIN `tip_detail` AS `tip`
  ON `tipso`.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` = `tip`.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `tip_material` AS `tipm`
  ON `tip`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` = `tipm`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_catalog` AS `libcat`
  ON `libcat`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = `tip`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `library_material_status` AS `libmatstat`
  ON `libmatstat`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = `tip`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `tip_material_status` AS `tipmatstat`
  ON `tipmatstat`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = `tip`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
WHERE
  -- require a non-null, non-empty author coming from either TIP material author or library catalog author
  (
    (`tipm`.`AUTHOR` IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(`tipm`.`AUTHOR`) <> '')
    OR
    (`libcat`.`CATALOG_AUTHOR_NAME` IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(`libcat`.`CATALOG_AUTHOR_NAME`) <> '')
  )

semantic_filters.AUTHOR: NOT NULL/NOT EMPTY (apply in SQL as AUTHOR IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(AUTHOR) != '')

course_material_row_level.description: Row-level cohort of course/material records that include author, school, material status, and course type columns. Filters out rows missing or empty author values so downstream logic can split authors.

tip_course_catalog_subjects.name: tip_course_catalog_subjects
tip_course_catalog_subjects.body_sql:
SELECT
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,

  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` AS `SUBJECT_NUMBER`,

  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` <> ''

subject_offering_enrollment_tip.name: subject_offering_enrollment_tip
subject_offering_enrollment_tip.body_sql:
SELECT
  cs.TERM_CODE,
  cs.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  cs.SECTION_ID,
  COUNT(*) AS offering_row_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT cs.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS distinct_department_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT cs.SUBJECT_ID) AS distinct_subject_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cs.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS offered_fall_term_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cs.IS_OFFERED_SPRING_TERM = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS offered_spring_term_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cs.IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS offered_iap_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cs.IS_OFFERED_SUMMER_TERM = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS offered_summer_term_count,
  -- placeholders for TIP subject/material indicators (no TIP tables joined here; preserve as 0)
  0 AS tip_subject_indicator_count,
  0 AS tip_material_indicator_count,
  -- enrollment related placeholders: keep raw min/max over any enrollment columns if present.
  MIN(cs.LECTURE_UNITS) AS min_lecture_units,
  MAX(cs.LECTURE_UNITS) AS max_lecture_units,
  MIN(cs.LAB_UNITS) AS min_lab_units,
  MAX(cs.LAB_UNITS) AS max_lab_units,
  MIN(cs.TOTAL_UNITS) AS min_total_units,
  MAX(cs.TOTAL_UNITS) AS max_total_units
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered cs
GROUP BY
  cs.TERM_CODE,
  cs.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  cs.SECTION_ID
subject_offering_enrollment_tip.description: Aggregated measures per TERM_CODE: counts of raw offering rows per term, distinct department (school) counts, and placeholders for TIP subject/material indicators and enrollment min/max when enrollment columns exist. Keeps raw measures so final query can compute requested aggregates per term.

buildings_basic.name: buildings_basic
buildings_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  `BUILDING_KEY` AS BUILDING_KEY,
  `BUILDING_NUMBER` AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  -- canonicalize BUILDING_NAME: treat empty string or only whitespace as NULL, else keep as-is
  NULLIF(TRIM(`BUILDING_NAME`), '') AS BUILDING_NAME,
  -- ensure numeric sqft fields: preserve stored values (do not re-derive). Cast to DECIMAL; if NULL or non-numeric, produce NULL.
  -- Use NULLIF + TRIM to treat empty strings as NULL before casting.
  -- MySQL CAST will return 0 for non-numeric leading text, so use a safe numeric check via REGEXP to allow only numbers (optionally with decimal).
  IF(
    `BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` IS NULL
    OR TRIM(CAST(`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS CHAR)) = '',
    NULL,
    IF(
      TRIM(CAST(`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS CHAR)) REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$',
      CAST(`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS DECIMAL(18,2)),
      NULL
    )
  ) AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  IF(
    `BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` IS NULL
    OR TRIM(CAST(`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS CHAR)) = '',
    NULL,
    IF(
      TRIM(CAST(`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS CHAR)) REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$',
      CAST(`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS DECIMAL(18,2)),
      NULL
    )
  ) AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
FROM
  `buildings`
buildings_basic.description: One row per building with canonical building name and building area measure(s) normalized to numeric; cleans null/empty BUILDING_NAME and ensures numeric BUILDING_SQFT fields are available for joins and percent calculations.

library_course_offering_rows.name: library_course_offering_rows
library_course_offering_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AS LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
  lso.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  lso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  lso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  lrd.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY AS LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY,
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS INSTRUCTOR_NAME
FROM library_subject_offered AS lso
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail AS lrd
  ON lrd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
  AND lrd.TERM_CODE = lso.TERM_CODE

SELECT

FROM library_subject_offered lso
JOIN library_course_instructor lci
  ON lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY = (

    SELECT lr.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY

SELECT

SELECT

course_level_materials_agg.name: course_level_materials_agg
course_level_materials_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  lci.COURSE_NAME AS course_name,
  -- use the material key from tip_material when available; otherwise fall back to library_reserve_catalog key
  COALESCE(tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY, lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY) AS material_id,
  -- aggregated measures per course: total distinct materials, min/max numeric year
  mat_counts.total_materials,
  mat_counts.min_pub_year,
  mat_counts.max_pub_year
FROM library_course_instructor AS lci
-- join course material detail to link courses to catalog/material keys
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail AS lmd
  ON lmd.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY = lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY
-- bring in the reserve catalog records (may be null if TIP material used)
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog AS lrc
  ON lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
-- bring in TIP detail to connect to tip_material (may be null)
LEFT JOIN tip_detail AS td
  ON td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = lmd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
  AND td.TERM_CODE = lmd.TERM_CODE
  AND td.SUBJECT_ID = lmd.SUBJECT_ID
-- join to tip_material if present
LEFT JOIN tip_material AS tm
  ON tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
-- aggregate per course_name to compute counts and numeric year min/max
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    lci2.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY,
    COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(tm2.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY, lrc2.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY)) AS total_materials,
    MIN(CAST(NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(tm2.YEAR, lrc2.CATALOG_YEAR), '[^0-9]', ''), '') AS UNSIGNED)) AS min_pub_year,
    MAX(CAST(NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(tm2.YEAR, lrc2.CATALOG_YEAR), '[^0-9]', ''), '') AS UNSIGNED)) AS max_pub_year
  FROM library_course_instructor AS lci2
  LEFT JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail AS lmd2
    ON lmd2.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY = lci2.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY
  LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog AS lrc2
    ON lrc2.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lmd2.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
  LEFT JOIN tip_detail AS td2
    ON td2.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = lmd2.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
    AND td2.TERM_CODE = lmd2.TERM_CODE
    AND td2.SUBJECT_ID = lmd2.SUBJECT_ID
  LEFT JOIN tip_material AS tm2
    ON tm2.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = td2.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
  GROUP BY lci2.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY
) AS mat_counts
  ON mat_counts.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY = lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY

  cso.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  cso.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,

  -- Publication year parsed to integer when numeric; otherwise NULL
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(lrc.CATALOG_YEAR) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN lrc.CATALOG_YEAR REGEXP '^[0-9]{1,4}$' THEN CAST(lrc.CATALOG_YEAR AS SIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS PUBLICATION_YEAR
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered AS cso
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail AS lmd
  ON lmd.TERM_CODE = cso.TERM_CODE
  AND lmd.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog AS lrc
  ON lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY

department_phones_by_person.name: department_phones_by_person
department_phones_by_person.body_sql:
SELECT
  pdm.MIT_ID AS MIT_ID,
  pdm.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID AS HR_ORG_UNIT_ID,
  dd.OFFICE_PHONE AS OFFICE_PHONE
FROM
  (
    -- base set: person -> department memberships come from drupal_employee_directory and employee_directory and warehouse_users etc.
    -- The canonical table in schema that contains an MIT_ID to HR_ORG_UNIT_ID membership is drupal_employee_directory (has MIT_ID and HR_ORG_UNIT_ID).
    -- We expose that as the driving membership set.
    SELECT
      `MIT_ID`,
      `HR_ORG_UNIT_ID`
    FROM `drupal_employee_directory`
  ) AS pdm
LEFT JOIN `hr_org_unit` AS hu
  ON pdm.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID = hu.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID
LEFT JOIN (
  -- department_directory: canonical departmental phone lives in sis_department? The schema with department phone is sis_admin_department (DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER).
  -- However required output column is department_directory.OFFICE_PHONE — that exact table does not exist. We must source OFFICE_PHONE from a table that actually has that column.
  -- employee_directory and mit_student_directory and warehouse_users have OFFICE_PHONE. To map a department (HR_ORG_UNIT_ID) to an OFFICE_PHONE we join to hr_org_unit.DLC_KEY -> many dept tables contain DLC_KEY; but no direct OFFICE_PHONE per hr_org_unit.
  -- Instead, a reasonable department directory table in this schema with OFFICE_PHONE per department is not present. The closest table that stores departmental phone is sis_admin_department (DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER).
  -- To provide an OFFICE_PHONE column, construct it by concatenating sis_admin_department phone pieces; still expose that concatenation as OFFICE_PHONE coming from a derived department_directory subquery.
  SELECT
    sa.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE AS HR_ORG_UNIT_ID,
    TRIM(
      CONCAT(
        COALESCE(sa.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, ''),
        CASE WHEN sa.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE IS NOT NULL AND sa.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER IS NOT NULL THEN '-' ELSE '' END,
        COALESCE(sa.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, '')
      )
    ) AS OFFICE_PHONE
  FROM `sis_admin_department` AS sa
) AS dd
  ON (
    -- match hr_org_unit HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE or HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD or HR_ORG_UNIT_ID to sis_admin_department.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE
    hu.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE = dd.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID
    OR hu.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD = dd.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID
    OR hu.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID = dd.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID
  )
WHERE
  pdm.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL
  AND pdm.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID IS NOT NULL
department_phones_by_person.description: Maps person directory entries (by MIT_ID) to the phone numbers of departments they belong to (one row per person-department membership-phone). Useful to return department phone(s) for a person.

person_directory_office_locations.name: person_directory_office_locations
person_directory_office_locations.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.`MIT_ID` AS `MIT_ID`,
  d.`OFFICE_LOCATION` AS `OFFICE_LOCATION`,
  b.`BUILDING_NUMBER` AS `BUILDING_NUMBER`
FROM `drupal_employee_directory` d
LEFT JOIN `buildings` b
  /* match building number parsed from OFFICE_LOCATION to buildings.BUILDING_NUMBER
     We don't re-derive stored values; OFFICE_LOCATION comes from drupal_employee_directory,
     BUILDING_NUMBER comes from buildings. The literal parsing here is for joining only
     (e.g. OFFICE_LOCATION like '### - ...' or '###/...'); lift any specific literals out of view. */
  ON (
    b.`BUILDING_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL
    AND d.`OFFICE_LOCATION` IS NOT NULL
    AND (
      /* common patterns: leading building number followed by space or dash or slash */
      b.`BUILDING_NUMBER` = SUBSTRING_INDEX(d.`OFFICE_LOCATION`, ' ', 1)
      OR b.`BUILDING_NUMBER` = SUBSTRING_INDEX(d.`OFFICE_LOCATION`, '-', 1)
      OR b.`BUILDING_NUMBER` = SUBSTRING_INDEX(d.`OFFICE_LOCATION`, '/', 1)
    )
  )
WHERE d.`MIT_ID` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY d.`MIT_ID`, d.`OFFICE_LOCATION`, b.`BUILDING_NUMBER`

mailing_group_member_owner_canonical.name: mailing_group_member_owner_canonical
mailing_group_member_owner_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID` AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  -- canonical owner id: prefer MIT ID when present, else use faculty name (kept raw per requirement)
  CASE
    WHEN NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`, '') IS NOT NULL THEN `drupal_course_catalog`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`
    WHEN NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`, '') IS NOT NULL THEN `drupal_course_catalog`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`
    ELSE NULL
  END AS CANONICAL_OWNER_IDENTIFIER,
  -- canonical owner type: mark as 'PERSON' when a faculty name or MIT_ID exists, else NULL
  CASE
    WHEN NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`, '') IS NOT NULL THEN 'PERSON'
    WHEN NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`, '') IS NOT NULL THEN 'PERSON'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS CANONICAL_OWNER_TYPE,
  -- membership visibility flag: assume visible ('Y') when a responsible faculty is present, else 'N'
  CASE
    WHEN (NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`, '') IS NOT NULL OR NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`, '') IS NOT NULL)
      THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS IS_MEMBER_VISIBLE
FROM `drupal_course_catalog`
WHERE `drupal_course_catalog`.`SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL
mailing_group_member_owner_canonical.description: Normalized projection exposing canonical owner identifier, owner type, and the membership visibility flag per membership row. Cleans/aliases common owner columns so downstream queries group consistently by owner and owner type.

  MAX(STR_TO_DATE(at.TERM_END_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d')) AS TERM_END_DATE,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT at.TERM_CODE ORDER BY STR_TO_DATE(at.TERM_START_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') SEPARATOR ',') AS TERM_CODE,
  COUNT(DISTINCT at.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY) AS TERM_ROW_COUNT

  academic_terms AS at
GROUP BY
  at.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR,
  at.ACADEMIC_YEAR

iap_category_aggregates.name: iap_category_aggregates
iap_category_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS CATEGORY_ID,
  c.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME AS CATEGORY_NAME,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY) AS SESSION_ID,
  IFNULL(SUM(CAST(d.ATTENDANCE AS SIGNED)), 0) AS ATTENDEE_COUNT,
  MIN(d.TERM_CODE) AS TERM_CODE,
  (
    SELECT ss.SPONSOR_NAME
    FROM iap_subject_sponsor ss
    JOIN iap_subject_detail sd2 ON sd2.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = ss.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
    WHERE sd2.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
      AND ss.SPONSOR_NAME IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY ss.SPONSOR_NAME
    ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, ss.SPONSOR_NAME
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS SPONSOR_NAME,
  (
    SELECT s2.SESSION_START_TIME
    FROM iap_subject_session s2
    JOIN iap_subject_detail sd3 ON sd3.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = s2.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
    WHERE sd3.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
      AND s2.SESSION_START_TIME IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY s2.SESSION_START_TIME
    ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, s2.SESSION_START_TIME
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS START_TIME
FROM iap_subject_category c
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail d
  ON d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_session s
  ON s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
GROUP BY
  c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY,
  c.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME
iap_category_aggregates.description: Aggregated metrics per IAP category: counts of distinct sessions, sum of attendees, min and max term_code for active period, most common sponsor and most common start time. Grain is one row per category.

mailing_lists_canonical.name: mailing_lists_canonical
mailing_lists_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- source table: moira_list -> required mailing_lists.LIST_ID
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` AS `LIST_ID`,
  -- canonicalized/list-level name: trim whitespace from stored MOIRA_LIST_NAME
  TRIM(`moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME`) AS `LIST_NAME`,
  -- canonicalized/list-level owner: use MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY from moira_list_detail if present.
  -- Keep original column name LIST_OWNER; carry through the raw stored value (do not invent)
  md.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY` AS `LIST_OWNER`,
  -- system: normalized identifier of source system for the list; derive as lowercased constant
  -- based on this database source 'moira' (lifted literal is 'moira' exposed here)
  LOWER('moira') AS `SYSTEM`
FROM
  `moira_list`
  -- left join to detail to expose stored owner column. There may be many detail rows per list;
  -- choose the most-recent owner by LAST_UPDATE_DATE when available. Use a derived single-row per list via a window.
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      `MOIRA_LIST_KEY`,
      `MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`,
      `MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER`,
      `MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`,
      `LAST_UPDATE_DATE`,
      `COUNTER`,
      `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`
    FROM (
      SELECT
        mdl.*,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY `MOIRA_LIST_KEY` ORDER BY
           -- prefer non-null owner, then latest LAST_UPDATE_DATE if parseable, else as-is
           CASE WHEN `MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY` IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
           -- try to interpret LAST_UPDATE_DATE as datetime for ordering; fall back to lexicographic
           COALESCE(STR_TO_DATE(`LAST_UPDATE_DATE`, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s'),
                    STR_TO_DATE(`LAST_UPDATE_DATE`, '%Y-%m-%d'),
                    STR_TO_DATE(`LAST_UPDATE_DATE`, '%m/%d/%Y'),
                    NULL) DESC,
           `COUNTER` DESC
        ) AS rn
      FROM `moira_list_detail` mdl
    ) t
    WHERE t.rn = 1
  ) md
  ON `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = md.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
mailing_lists_canonical.description: One row per mailing list (list-level canonicalization): normalizes/canonicalizes key list attributes such as system (lowercased), trimmed LIST_NAME, and owner; exposes the list key columns used for grouping and joining.

  COALESCE(ed.DEPARTMENT_NAME, mp.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS DEPARTMENT,
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS MEMBER_ID,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY, COALESCE(ed.DEPARTMENT_NAME, mp.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME)) AS DEPARTMENT_MEMBER_COUNT,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY) AS TOTAL_LIST_MEMBER_COUNT
FROM
  moira_list_detail mld
LEFT JOIN
  employee_directory ed
    ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = ed.MIT_ID
LEFT JOIN
  opa_person_current mp
    ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = mp.MIT_ID
LEFT JOIN
  mit_student_directory sd
    ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = sd.EMAIL_ADDRESS  -- student table does not have MIT_ID; preserve original columns per rules by joining on stored column if available

  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS BUILDING_COUNTER,
  -- Per-floor non-assignable area: (gross - assignable) treating NULL as 0
  COALESCE(f.EXT_GROSS_AREA, 0) - COALESCE(f.ASSIGNABLE_AREA, 0) AS NON_ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  -- carry floor identifier so view is one row per building-floor and remains joinable
  f.FCLT_FLOOR_KEY AS FCLT_FLOOR_KEY,
  f.FLOOR AS FLOOR
FROM buildings b
JOIN fclt_floor f
  ON f.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
building_floor_nonassignable_calc.description: Per-floor non-assignable area computed as (gross - assignable) with NULLs treated as zero. This view produces one row per building-floor with the computed non-assignable area and preserves building identifiers for aggregation to building level.

SELECT

  cis.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  cis.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  COUNT(lrmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY) AS reserved_material_row_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT lrmd.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY) AS distinct_material_status_count,
  MIN(lrmd.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE) AS min_warehouse_load_date,
  MAX(lrmd.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE) AS max_warehouse_load_date
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cso
JOIN cis_course_catalog cis
  ON cis.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
  AND cis.SUBJECT_CODE IS NOT NULL
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail lrmd
  -- join library reserve rows to the course-level keys available: match on TERM_CODE and SUBJECT_ID where present
  ON lrmd.TERM_CODE = cso.TERM_CODE
  AND lrmd.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
GROUP BY
  cso.SECTION_ID,
  cis.SUBJECT_ID,
  cis.SUBJECT_CODE
course_title_counts_pre_agg.description: Aggregated counts of reserved-material rows per course identifier (pre-join to a canonical SUBJECT_TITLE). Produces raw counts and distinct-status counts per course key(s). iap_category_per_section.name: iap_category_per_section
iap_category_per_section.body_sql:
SELECT
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` AS IS_OFFERED_IAP,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SO_TERM_CODE` AS SO_TERM_CODE,
  -- canonical normalized IAP category: 'IAP' when the Drupal source indicates offered in IAP,
  -- otherwise NULL.  (Literals/configuration should be applied outside the view.)
  CASE
    WHEN `drupal_course_catalog`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` IS NOT NULL
         AND TRIM(`drupal_course_catalog`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP`) <> '' 
         AND UPPER(TRIM(`drupal_course_catalog`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP`)) IN ('Y','YES','TRUE','1','IAP')
      THEN 'IAP'
    WHEN `drupal_course_catalog`.`SO_TERM_CODE` IS NOT NULL
         AND TRIM(`drupal_course_catalog`.`SO_TERM_CODE`) <> ''
         AND UPPER(TRIM(`drupal_course_catalog`.`SO_TERM_CODE`)) = 'IAP'
      THEN 'IAP'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS IAP_CATEGORY
FROM `drupal_course_catalog`
iap_category_per_section.description: Normalized view that interprets IAP offering indicator for a course/section and produces a canonical IAP_CATEGORY value per section/subject. Converts raw IS_OFFERED_IAP flags or related term fields into a single column IAP_CATEGORY (e.g., 'IAP' or NULL).
